correctness.rationale: In the ideal interaction frame the overlap derivative with the input ray is minus the integrated jump variance. For the lab jump |0><1| at a pure state with excited population p it is p−p(1−p)=p², so 4K± are the integrals of (1∓z)². The polar angle is absolutely continuous and |θ′|≤Ω. For every continuous f≥0, integrate the derivative of its polar-angle antiderivative to obtain Ω∫f(θ)dt≥∫f(θ)θ′dt=∫_0^π f(s)ds. Hence the residence measure minus ds/Ω is positive, of mass Δ, and the common baseline is C. At Δ=0 this proves the singleton. For Δ>0 the moments of X=cosθ under normalized residual mass satisfy h²≤q≤1, equivalent to the claimed inequalities. For h<1 an independent representation uses a=(h−q)/(1−h) and mass (h−a)/(1−a) at +1 with the rest at a; for h=1 take X=1. Maximum-speed meridian travel plus those dwells realizes all pairs by piecewise-constant control. Then 4K+≥C and 4K−≤C+4Δ. Equality with Δ>0 forces residual time entirely at the north pole: the angular crossing spends at least π/Ω in the open band, exactly its total residence there, and must be a shortest maximum-speed meridian. No extra pole-to-interior excursion or south-pole wait remains possible. originality.rationale: The general first-order variance/moment identity and the pole wait–flip–wait family are covered by Patra. In particular the one-sided pole wait and its fixed-bath achievable ratio are not standalone new results. The supported distinct claim is the exact jointly attainable region for every speed-capped ideal inversion under the fixed bath, including a global converse, the non-polar boundary, and two-dwell achievability. The inspected prior formulas do not classify which moments are feasible at fixed T and Ω.
residual_risks: No exhaustive priority claim; the inspected Patra passages are not a claim about every line of that paper.
The pole extremizer and variance law are credited to the existing framework, not accepted as independent originality here.
